Definition: from G1656; to compassionate (by word or deed, specially, by divine grace):--have compassion (pity on), have (obtain, receive, shew) mercy (on).
BiblicalUsage: eleéō turns up where the Bible says to have mercy, to have compassion. In Matthew 5:7, the text says "for they shall obtain mercy." In Matthew 9:27, the text says "have mercy on us."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that eleéō matters because God's mercy is not a vague feeling but something He does — He sees need, and He acts on it. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Sermon on the Mount; Jesus Heals Two Blind Men
